annotator.notes: Student makes a common mistake by calculating based on one ingredient without checking the limiting factor. Tutor guides them to find the limiting ingredient first.

task_context.problem_statement: Blake wants to spend his Friday making milkshakes for his family. He knows that he needs 4 ounces of milk and 12 ounces of ice cream for each milkshake. If he has 72 ounces of milk and 192 ounces of ice cream, how much milk will be left over when he is done?
task_context.reference_solution:
He has enough milk to make 18 milkshakes because 72 / 4 = <<72/4=18>>18
He has enough ice cream to make 16 milkshakes because 192 / 12 = <<192/12=16>>16
He can only make 16 milkshakes because 16 < 18
He will use 64 ounces of milk because 16 x 4 = <<16*4=64>>64
He will have 8 ounces of milk left because 72 - 64 = <<72-64=8>>8
#### 8

messages.content: I'm stuck on this problem: Blake wants to spend his Friday making milkshakes for his family. He knows that he needs 4 ounces of milk and 12 ounces of ice cream for each milkshake. If he has 72 ounces of milk and 192 ounces of ice cream, how much milk will be left over when he is done? I think the answer is 0 because 72 divided by 4 is 18, so he uses all the milk. Is that right?

I see how you got that! You calculated how many milkshakes he could make if he only had to worry about the milk. However, remember that each milkshake also requires ice cream. Do you think he has enough ice cream to make all 18 milkshakes?
Oh, I didn't think about that. Let me check. 18 milkshakes times 12 ounces of ice cream... that's 216 ounces. But he only has 192 ounces. So he can't make 18.
Exactly. Since he runs out of ice cream first, he won't be able to use all the milk. Based on the amount of ice cream he actually has, how many full milkshakes can he make?
If he has 192 ounces and each one takes 12, then 192 / 12 is 16. So he can only make 16 milkshakes.
That's correct. Now that we know he can only make 16 milkshakes, how much of the milk will he actually use up?
16 milkshakes times 4 ounces of milk each is 64 ounces. So he uses 64 ounces of milk.
You've got it. Now, for the final step: if he started with 72 ounces of milk and used 64, how much is left over?
72 minus 64 is 8. So there are 8 ounces of milk left over!
Spot on! You correctly identified that the ice cream was the limiting factor, which changed how much milk was used. Great job working through that.
